description: Ballot-paper party labels that Browse lists under their party instead of as parties of their own (scripts/build-browse-indexes.mjs, partyLabelFolds). Each label is matched exactly against a canonical_name in data/elections-source/data/party-ids.json and folded into the party whose id is the key. Only a label that is plainly the same party belongs here: a misspelling, the party's other name, the leader's name or the candidate's occupation printed in the party field. Coalitions, independents and splinter groups that carry a party's name are different parties and are listed under neverFold, which also stops the automatic misspelling match. The old address of a folded label still opens its party (previousSlugs). Every fold is printed by the build and written to data/browse/party-label-folds.json. retiredSlugs lists the addresses of party pages that are no longer built because their candidacies now carry another party's label (a source-checked relabel or a registry merge); each still opens the party it is listed under. Batch 4c (2026-11-06): the party-ids.json labels are a scan of the source rows of 25 May 2026, when the 1973-2011 council results still carried ARK's ballot descriptions (party and occupation side by side, OCR slips, a party's name printed twice); those rows have since been replaced, so no candidacy carries these labels and every interpreted label in the results is a party. Each such label is folded into the party the same candidacies read as in the results (an occupation alone into the candidate's party, usually Independent), or, where a label names a party the results read less precisely, into that party with the source cited. tests/elections/party-label-occupations.test.mjs fails when a listed label has an occupation, a misspelt party name or a party named twice.

independent.reason: independents whose ballot paper gave an occupation, an office or an honour with or without the word Independent, or a misspelt Independent; each candidacy reads Independent in the results (batch 4c). An occupation is never a party label: it stays only in the label as printed
